sections.title: Amplitude: API key and server zone
sections.summary: Paste the API Key from your Amplitude project Settings, then pick the server zone (US, or EU for GDPR data residency) that matches where your Amplitude project lives — the wrong zone means events never arrive. You can also turn on session start/end tracking to capture session lifecycle events.

sections.title: Custom Script: HEAD and BODY
sections.summary: For tools without a built-in option, add your own JavaScript at two points: code in HEAD runs before the page renders (load SDKs here), and code in BODY runs after it loads (attach handlers here). Call window.segmentlySDK.setCustomData(key, value) to hand funnel data to your script. Reach for this only when no built-in provider above fits.

sections.title: Facebook (Meta) Pixel: Pixel ID
sections.summary: Paste the Pixel ID from Meta Events Manager so your funnel and checkout events attribute back to your Facebook and Instagram ad campaigns. Optionally turn on auto-config to also capture button clicks and page metadata without extra setup.

sections.title: Google Analytics 4: Measurement ID
sections.summary: Paste your Measurement ID (it looks like G-XXXXXXXXXX). Find it in GA4 under Admin then Data Streams then your web stream. It routes every funnel event to the correct GA4 property; if the format is wrong, Segmently blocks the save so a typo can't silently break tracking.

sections.title: Google Tag Manager: Container ID
sections.summary: Paste your Container ID (it looks like GTM-XXXXX) from Google Tag Manager. Segmently pushes every funnel event into the dataLayer, so your existing GTM triggers and tags fire on them. Only set a custom Data Layer name if your container was specifically built to expect a non-default one.

sections.title: Name the integration
sections.summary: Enter a clear label such as 'GA4 Production' or 'Amplitude EU'. It only appears in your own integrations list and edit menus to help you tell destinations apart — visitors never see it. Pick a name that says which tool and which environment it points at.

sections.title: Mixpanel: project token
sections.summary: Paste the Project Token from your Mixpanel project Settings, then choose where it's stored on the visitor's browser (localStorage by default, or Cookie if your setup needs it). You can also enable page-view tracking if you want each screen view recorded automatically.

sections.title: PostHog: project token and region
sections.summary: Paste the Project Token — that's the API key, not the numeric Project ID — found in PostHog under Settings then General. Then pick your region: US Cloud, EU Cloud, or Self-Hosted. If you chose Self-Hosted, also enter your own PostHog API host URL so events know where to go.

sections.title: Server-side analytics (Conversions API, GA4 Measurement Protocol, and more)
sections.summary: Server-side destinations send payment events straight from Segmently's servers — purchase, subscription, cancellation, and failure only — for revenue attribution that ad-blockers and browser limits can't drop. They use the same credentials as the matching client pixel but do not receive engagement events (screen views, button taps), so run them alongside the client pixel to track the full funnel.

sections.title: TikTok Pixel: Pixel ID
sections.summary: Paste the Pixel ID (it looks like CXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX) from TikTok Ads Manager under Events. Under Advanced Matching you can optionally pass hashed email and phone, which improves how reliably TikTok attributes conversions back to your ads.

sections.title: Amplitude API key and server zone
sections.summary: In Amplitude open Settings, Projects, select the project: copy the API Key into the Amplitude integration and pick the zone from your organisation URL (analytics.eu.amplitude.com means EU). Verify against the live vendor UI before publishing.
sections.verifyHint: Amplitude User Look-Up finds a user from the published funnel URL.

sections.title: GA4 Measurement Protocol API secret
sections.summary: In the same web stream open Measurement Protocol API secrets and click Create; paste the secret into the GA4 Measurement Protocol (server) integration. Verify against the live vendor UI before publishing.
sections.verifyHint: GA4 DebugView shows the server-sent event.

sections.title: GA4 Measurement ID
sections.summary: In Google Analytics open Admin, Data streams, select the web stream: the Measurement ID (starts with G-) is at the top right. Paste it into the GA4 integration. Verify against the live vendor UI before publishing.
sections.verifyHint: GA4 Realtime report shows a user from the published funnel URL.

sections.title: Mixpanel project token and service account
sections.summary: In Mixpanel open Project Settings, Access Keys: copy the Project Token into the Mixpanel integration. For the server integration create a service account under Organization, Service Accounts and paste its username and secret together with the project id. Verify against the live vendor UI before publishing.
sections.verifyHint: Mixpanel Events → Live view shows the funnel events.

sections.title: PostHog project API key and host
sections.summary: In PostHog open Project Settings: copy the Project API key (starts with phc_) into the PostHog integration and set the host that matches your region (US or EU cloud, or your self-hosted URL). Verify against the live vendor UI before publishing.
sections.verifyHint: PostHog Live events shows the funnel events.
